problem: A student can read 'no contention cost' as 'contention does not exist in PRAM', which then contradicts Section 2, where concurrent access to the same cell is exactly what EREW, CREW and CRCW restrict.
fix: Say: 'Every access costs 1 time unit however many processors use the memory, so there is no extra penalty for contention; but the variant still decides who may access the same cell in one step.'

where: Section 1 formula and Worked example 1, step 3
problem: The chapter equates cost with work, then charges all P processors for every round. In the tree combine only 4, then 2, then 1 processors are active, so the real work is 7 combines, while 'cost' by the definition C = T × P is 24. The two numbers measure different things and a student will confuse them.
fix: Keep C = T × P as the definition, and add: 'P is charged for every round even when some processors sit idle; the number of combine operations actually performed here is 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.'

problem: 'EREW must serialise a CRCW write conflict' suggests one-writer-at-a-time, which would take P rounds, and then the same paragraph says the tree does it in ⌈log₂ P⌉ rounds. The word and the number disagree.
fix: Write: 'EREW cannot let several processors touch the cell in the same step, so the conflict must be resolved before the write, for example by a tree combine.'

problem: 'Cost 1000 also means the parallel work equals 1000 sequential steps in the model, which bounds useful speedup' mixes processor-time with sequential steps and is only true if every processor is busy in all 10 steps. The correct bound needs the sequential run time T₁.
fix: Answer: 'Speedup is bounded by S ≤ T₁ / C, with T₁ the best known sequential time. Here C = 1000 processor-time units, so unless T₁ is much larger than 1000, the parallel version buys little; and cost 1000 assumes all 100 processors were busy in each of the 10 steps.'

problem: The question states the answer inside itself ('while EREW simulation costs O(log P)') and 'EREW simulation' is ambiguous about which direction is simulated.
fix: Ask: 'A single CRCW step is simulated on EREW in O(log P) time, while an EREW step needs no extra time on CRCW. Why?'
